title: The Painted Verdict
premise: Xanthe Ravensworth, archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent two decades cataloguing the town of Marrowgate's secrets from behind a locked crypt door. A stranger's advance payment hires him to prove that a murder has not yet happened — the murder of the stranger himself, predicted in a confession letter sealed in the crypt twenty years ago. As Xanthe investigates, he uncovers a conspiracy reaching into the cathedral chapter and the town council, where powerful men have been quietly eliminating anyone who threatens their hold on Marrowgate. In the end, Xanthe must choose between exposing the truth and preserving his own invisibility, and he discovers that justice outside the law demands a verdict written in his own hand — one that costs him the crypt, the archive, and nearly his life, but frees the town at last.
about_author: Emrys Brightwater is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years transcribing centuries-old ledgers before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about quiet people who know too much, and lives somewhere within sight of an old church tower.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Establishes Xanthe's ordered world: the crypt archive, its locked door, and his meticulous filing of Marrowgate's secrets. He takes quiet pride in knowing everything and being known by no one. Emotional beat: contentment built on avoidance.

chapters.title: Payment in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A gaunt stranger named Corwin Hale arrives after hours, pays triple to commission proof that his own murder will not happen — citing a sealed confession letter deposited in the crypt in 1987. Emotional beat: unease; the first crack in Xanthe's invisibility.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe retrieves the sealed deposit and finds it names four men — now the cathedral dean, the mayor, a magistrate, and a dead man — as future murderers. The letter predicts Hale's death 'when the bells fall silent.' Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. He interviews the town constable, who insists the case the letter references — the drowning of a girl named Ivy Marsh in 1987 — was closed as accidental. Everyone repeats the phrase 'closed for good' too smoothly. Emotional beat: the smell of a cover-up.

chapters.title: Bells Falling Silent
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The cathedral's bell-ringer resigns abruptly; maintenance on the bells begins, meaning they will be silent for weeks — exactly when the letter's deadline falls. Someone is following the letter's script. Emotional beat: cold realization.

chapters.title: The Client Vanishes
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Hale stops answering letters. Xanthe finds Hale's rented room searched and a threatening note left behind. The murder hasn't happened yet — but someone is preparing for it. Emotional beat: fear for another person, unfamiliar to him.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Digging through 1987 records, Xanthe finds pages razored out of the parish ledger — by someone with archive access. Only three people ever had keys: himself, the old archivist, and Dean Ambrose Vellacott. Emotional beat: betrayal close to home.

chapters.title: The Old Archivist's Hands
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe visits his predecessor, dying in a care home, who whispers that he cut out the pages to protect someone he loved — and begs Xanthe to let the past stay buried. Emotional beat: pity warring with resolve.

chapters.title: Ivy Marsh Was Real
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe tracks down Ivy Marsh's mother, who never believed the drowning verdict. She gives him Ivy's diary, hidden in a hymnal for thirty-seven years. Emotional beat: grief that has calcified into purpose.

chapters.title: The Diary's First Half
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The diary reveals Ivy was blackmailing a powerful man over something she witnessed in the crypt. Entries stop mid-sentence days before her death. Emotional beat: intimacy with a dead girl's voice.

chapters.title: A Warning in Wax
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A candle in Xanthe's office burns down around a message: STOP THE FILE. His lock was not forced — someone used a key. Emotional beat: violation; his sanctuary is no longer safe.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe approaches Magistrate Odile Ferrant, one of the letter's named four, expecting denial. Instead she warns him, obliquely, to drop it — and slips him a name. Emotional beat: ambiguity; even the guilty are trapped.

chapters.title: The Name Under the Name
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The name leads to Aldous Crane, the 'dead' fourth man — alive, hidden, living under a false identity in a coastal village. Crane was the witness Ivy protected. Emotional beat: hope with sharp edges.

chapters.title: Crane's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Crane (flashback frame). Crane recounts 1987: he saw the mayor's brother kill Ivy in the crypt and fled rather than testify, letting the old archivist take the blame's shadow. Emotional beat: shame as a life sentence.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Garden Party
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe infiltrates Mayor Roscoe Vane's garden party and observes the power network firsthand — Vane, Dean Vellacott, and business interests entwined like roots. Emotional beat: revulsion at how corruption wears charm.

chapters.title: The Brother in the Tower
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe identifies Vane's brother Merrick, officially 'gone abroad,' actually living in the cathedral close as a lay steward — the man with a key and no history. Emotional beat: the killer has been beside him all along.

chapters.title: Hale Resurfaces
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Hale contacts Xanthe from hiding: he is Ivy's cousin, and the letter was his gambit to force the truth open before Merrick silences him too. Emotional beat: alliance forged in mutual fear.

chapters.title: Twenty Years Invisible
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Interlude: Xanthe confronts why he chose the crypt — a family scandal of his own he filed away instead of facing. Emotional beat: recognition that his invisibility was always a kind of complicity.

chapters.title: The Copy That Counts
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe makes duplicate evidence sets — diary, letter, ledger reconstruction — and hides them in three places, learning from the archive's own lesson: nothing true should exist in only one copy. Emotional beat: methodical courage.

chapters.title: Silence Ordered
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The bishop, pressured from above, suspends Xanthe from the archive pending an 'audit.' His key is revoked. Emotional beat: the machinery of power closing around him.

chapters.title: Breaking Into My Own Life
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe uses the old archivist's forgotten second key to enter the crypt at night and photograph what remains. He finds fresh mortar on one wall niche — recently resealed. Emotional beat: defiance sharpening into recklessness.

chapters.title: Behind Fresh Mortar
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The niche holds Ivy Marsh's remains — she was never in the river at all. The 'drowning' was staged. Emotional beat: horror; the closed case was closed over a body.

chapters.title: The Constable's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe confronts the aging constable, who confesses he falsified the 1987 report under pressure and has hated himself since. He agrees to swear a statement. Emotional beat: a broken man choosing, late, to stand.

chapters.title: Merrick Makes Contact
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Merrick Vane offers Xanthe money, then threats, revealing he knows about Crane and Hale. He gives Xanthe until the bells are rehung to hand over everything. Emotional beat: terror worn as a mask of calm.

chapters.title: Hale Is Taken
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Hale disappears again — this time taken. A taunting note proves Merrick has him alive, bait to draw out Xanthe and the diary. Emotional beat: guilt; his investigation endangered the innocent.

chapters.title: The Choice of Weapons
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe weighs law against justice: the constable's statement could vanish into Ferrant's court; the press could be bought; Vane owns the town's institutions. Emotional beat: the theme made explicit — what does justice cost, and who pays?

chapters.title: Ferrant's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Ferrant offers a deal: give her the evidence quietly and she'll bury Merrick alone, sparing the institution. Xanthe realizes she wants the conspiracy contained, not exposed. Emotional beat: temptation of the half-truth.

chapters.title: The Bells Are Rehung
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The restoration finishes; the bells ring again, and the letter's deadline expires — but nothing happens. Xanthe understands the deadline was never prophecy; it was a schedule set by the killers themselves. Emotional beat: clarity through the noise.

chapters.title: Trap in the Crypt
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Following a staged clue, Xanthe enters the crypt at night and is locked in with Hale, unconscious but alive. Merrick intends a fire to end both, mirroring the original cover-up. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair.

chapters.title: Verdict by Candlelight
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Trapped, Xanthe uses the crypt's own architecture — the ventilation flue behind the archive shelves — to smoke-signal the bell-ringers below. Emotional beat: the invisible man using invisibility as a weapon.

chapters.title: Fire and Bell
chapters.summary: POV multiple, brief. The bell-ringers raise the alarm; the town watches the cathedral smoke while Vane tries to control the narrative publicly. Merrick flees into the close. Emotional beat: a town waking up.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Close
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe, burned and coughing, pursues Merrick across the rooftops of the cathedral close. Merrick falls from the bell tower — whether pushed or slipped, Xanthe will never say. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in moral gray.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Long Night
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. With Merrick dead, Xanthe delivers the full evidence not to Ferrant but to a national journalist and the diocesan tribunal simultaneously, making burial impossible. Vane is arrested at dawn. Emotional beat: cold triumph.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The tribunal hearings: the constable testifies, Crane comes out of hiding, and Ivy's mother finally hears the truth of her daughter's death. Emotional beat: grief given its day in the light.

chapters.title: What Justice Doesn't Return
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The fallout: the cathedral is disgraced, the archive sealed by investigators, and Xanthe — celebrated outside, suspect inside — loses the only home he had. Emotional beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: Ferrant's Resignation
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Ferrant resigns and tells Xanthe privately that he did right, and that she would have done wrong, and she cannot forgive either of them. Emotional beat: mercy without absolution.

chapters.title: The Last Filing
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Allowed one final hour in the crypt, Xanthe files the whole case — every document, including his own compromises — under M for Marsh, closing it honestly this time. Emotional beat: ritual as redemption.

chapters.title: A Door Left Open
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe leaves Marrowgate, giving his key not to a successor chosen by the chapter but to Ivy's mother, keeper of the truth now. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: The Painted Verdict
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe, epistolary coda. Months later, a restored fresco in the cathedral is unveiled — painted over the crypt wall, depicting Ivy among the saints. Xanthe reads about it in a newspaper far away. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: New Client, New Key
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. In a new town, Xanthe has begun a small archive of his own — honest, unlocked. A nervous visitor knocks with a secret. He opens the door. Emotional beat: the invisible man chooses to be found.
